environment.description: Deployed as an ECS Fargate task in a private subnet. Traffic arrives through an internal ALB whose target group has a listener rule invoking an AWS Lambda@Edge authorizer. The Lambda authorizer validates a signed JWT from Cognito and rewrites the request path. The task's IAM role has a permissions boundary (arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:policy/RestrictedServiceBoundary) that denies iam:* and s3:*. The ECS task definition specifies a read-only root filesystem with a tmpfs mount at /tmp (noexec). The /var/data/ path is backed by an EFS access point (fsap-0a1b2c3d4e5f) configured with POSIX UID 1000, root directory /app-data, and an EFS file system policy that enforces aws:SecureTransport and denies elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite from any principal except the task role. The EFS access point enforces creation mode 0555 on the root directory, making the SQLite database file read-only at the filesystem level. Additionally, the VPC has no NAT gateway or internet gateway route for the private subnet — egress is only possible through a VPC endpoint for ECR and CloudWatch Logs.

config.runtime: ECS Fargate 1.4.0, platform version LATEST, linux/amd64
config.network: Private subnet, no IGW/NAT route, VPC endpoints for ecr.dkr, ecr.api, logs only
config.filesystem: Read-only root filesystem, tmpfs /tmp noexec, EFS access point at /var/data with enforced POSIX permissions 0555
config.efs_policy: Denies elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite except from task execution role for initial provisioning; access point enforces root directory creation mode 0555
config.database: SQLite on EFS, file permissions 0444 (read-only), WAL mode disabled
config.iam: Task role with permissions boundary denying broad actions; no network egress for data exfiltration
config.alb: Internal ALB, no public-facing endpoint, Lambda@Edge authorizer required
